# FounderConsole

> FounderConsole is an AI decision simulator for startup founders and D2C (direct-to-consumer)
> brands. It connects your company's financial data, runs Monte Carlo simulations, and answers
> runway, burn, contribution margin and fundraising questions with probability ranges
> (P10/P50/P90) instead of a single spreadsheet forecast. Free during public beta; no credit
> card required.

Who it is for: founders and finance leads of Indian D2C and Shopify brands who track
contribution margin (CM1/CM2/CM3), RTO and COD, ad spend and MER, inventory, cash and
runway in rupees (lakh/crore); and startup founders generally who need runway, burn and
fundraising answers.

FounderConsole publishes the benchmarks and formulas it uses, so its pages can be quoted
directly. The figures in "Citable facts" below are the ones the site itself publishes.
Last updated: 2026-11-12.

## Citable facts and formulas

- Runway = Cash balance / Net monthly burn.
- Burn multiple = Net burn / Net new ARR. Published bands: elite under 1x, good 1-1.5x,
  acceptable 1.5-2x, concerning above 2x; above 3x is a hard fundraising signal.
- Runway guidance: target 18-24 months after a raise, never let it fall below 12 months,
  and treat under 6 months as an emergency.
- Start a fundraise with 9-12 months of runway left: enough to build a data room, meet
  30-50 investors and close, without the weak negotiating position that urgency creates.
- Series A readiness for SaaS, as published: $1M+ ARR, growing roughly 3x year over year,
  and 9-12 months of runway.
- Other published health bands: net revenue retention elite above 120%; monthly churn
  best-in-class under 1%; LTV:CAC excellent above 5x; CAC payback excellent under 6 months;
  SaaS gross margin best-in-class 80% or higher.
- Pricing, as published on /pricing: every feature is free during the public beta
  (early access). No credit card is required, and no plan is charged yet. Paid
  tiers come later.

## D2C finance: definitions and formulas

Definitions FounderConsole uses for D2C brands (also on
https://founderconsole.ai/tools/d2c-contribution-margin):

- Net revenue = value of orders delivered and kept, excluding GST, after discounts.
  RTO (return to origin) orders and customer returns are not revenue.
- CM1 (contribution margin 1) = net revenue - COGS.
- CM2 = CM1 - fulfilment (forward shipping, packaging, reverse shipping on RTO and
  returns) - payment costs (gateway fees on prepaid orders, COD fees).
- CM3 = CM2 - marketing (ads, influencers, affiliates). CM3 is what orders contribute
  to fixed costs and profit; if CM3 is negative, growth increases the loss.
- MER (marketing efficiency ratio) = net revenue / total marketing spend. Unlike platform
  ROAS, it cannot be inflated by attribution or double counting.
- Break-even MER = 1 / CM2 margin. Below it, marketing loses money at CM3.
- D2C runway = cash / monthly cash burn, where cash burn = fixed costs - CM3 + net
  inventory build + growth in COD remittances and marketplace payouts owed to you.

Worked example (illustrative brand, not a benchmark): Rs 1,200 AOV ex-GST, 2,000 orders a
month, 18% RTO, 5% returns, 55% COD, Rs 420 COGS, Rs 70 shipping each way, Rs 30 packaging,
2% gateway fee, Rs 40 COD fee, Rs 6 lakh marketing. Net revenue Rs 18.70 lakh; CM1 Rs 12.15
lakh (65.0%); CM2 Rs 9.27 lakh (49.6%); CM3 Rs 3.27 lakh (17.5%), about Rs 199 per delivered
order; MER 3.12x vs break-even MER 2.02x. At 30% RTO, CM3 falls to Rs 1.38 lakh. In this
example each percentage point of RTO costs about Rs 15,700 of CM3 a month.

FounderConsole does not publish industry benchmark percentages for Indian D2C margins
because no sourced, dated dataset backs the figures that usually circulate.

## Built for your business

One page per kind of business, each with the numbers that business runs on:

- [D2C & e-commerce](https://founderconsole.ai/for/d2c): CM1, CM2 and CM3 per order in
  rupees, the cost of RTO and COD, MER, and the runway that inventory leaves.
- [SaaS / B2B software](https://founderconsole.ai/for/saas): MRR, ARR, churn, net revenue
  retention, burn multiple and CAC payback, with runway to the next round.
- [Marketplace / platform](https://founderconsole.ai/for/marketplace): GMV separated from
  take rate and net revenue, supply and demand incentives, contribution per order.
- [Agency / services](https://founderconsole.ai/for/agency): utilisation, project margins,
  the gap between invoicing and getting paid, and whether the next hire is affordable.
- [Fintech](https://founderconsole.ai/for/fintech): per-user unit economics, LTV against
  CAC, CAC payback and the regulatory capital requirement, with runway stress tests.
- [Early-stage / pre-revenue](https://founderconsole.ai/for/startup): runway and burn,
  hiring plans, and the fundraising timeline as a range rather than a single date.

## Free tools

- [Startup Runway Calculator](https://founderconsole.ai/tools/runway-calculator): enter cash
  on hand, monthly revenue, expenses and growth rate to see months of runway remaining and
  the month the cash runs out.
- [D2C Contribution Margin Calculator](https://founderconsole.ai/tools/d2c-contribution-margin):
  CM1, CM2 and CM3 per order in rupees from AOV, RTO rate, COD share, COGS, shipping and
  marketing, with MER and break-even MER. Runs in the browser; nothing is stored.
- [Burn Multiple Calculator](https://founderconsole.ai/tools/burn-multiple),
  [Dilution Calculator](https://founderconsole.ai/tools/dilution) and
  [LTV:CAC Calculator](https://founderconsole.ai/tools/ltv-cac). All free tools:
  https://founderconsole.ai/tools
- [Default Alive or Default Dead](https://founderconsole.ai/default-alive): Paul Graham's
  test, answered in 30 seconds - at current growth and current expenses, do you reach
  profitability before the money runs out?
- [Startup Survival Simulator](https://founderconsole.ai/survival-simulator): Monte Carlo
  survival probability with shareable results.
- [Runway benchmarks by industry](https://founderconsole.ai/runway/saas): SaaS, ecommerce,
  fintech, marketplace, AI, hardware, biotech and devtools, each with its own benchmark
  runway and typical burn and revenue inputs.

## Product

- [AI Copilot](https://founderconsole.ai/ai-cfo): multi-agent router/orchestrator that reads
  your company data and returns ranked decision recommendations.
- [Fundraising OS](https://founderconsole.ai/features): cap table management, dilution
  modelling, investor CRM, SAFE conversion and exit waterfall analysis.
- [Monte Carlo simulation engine](https://founderconsole.ai/product): 24-month probabilistic
  projections with P10/P50/P90 confidence bands, scenario versioning and sensitivity analysis.
- [Digital Twin](https://founderconsole.ai/how-it-works): a continuously updated model of the
  company with health scoring and risk indicators.
- [Integrations](https://founderconsole.ai/features): 36 read-only data connectors including
  Stripe, QuickBooks, Xero, Mercury, Brex, Plaid, Gusto, HubSpot, Shopify and Salesforce.
- [Pricing](https://founderconsole.ai/pricing) - [Security](https://founderconsole.ai/security)
  - [FAQ](https://founderconsole.ai/faq) - [Demo](https://founderconsole.ai/demo)

preparation, burn rate and unit economics, SaaS metrics, and board reporting.
